batches.description: Sources batch 5: public-API parameter boundaries and link-header parse calls

label.rationale: GiftCard.redeem builds redemption_path = '%s/redeem' % self.redemption_code (line 456) and joins it onto self._url or base_uri (lines 459/461). redemption_code occupies the FIRST path position, so a scheme-prefixed value (e.g. 'http://evil.com/redeem') makes urljoin return an absolute URL, replacing scheme and host - genuine host-forgery capability if the attribute is attacker-influenced. The attribute is set by the embedding application (constructor kwargs) or parsed from the server response; the account_code parameter goes to the request body only. Boundary = embedding application; needs host-app context review.

add_on_code is interpolated into the trailing slots of '%s/add_ons/%s' % (self.plan_code, add_on_code) (line 1176): the urljoin path argument always STARTS with self.plan_code, so this parameter alone cannot introduce an absolute URL or change scheme/host/port - path-only control, which is not CWE-918 host forgery. (Residual first-slot plan_code risk is recorded on the create_add_on summary entry.)

Externally delivered Recurly push-notification body: the host application feeds the raw webhook POST body into this function and the SDK parses it with ElementTree.fromstring WITHOUT any signature verification. The decoded Resource elements carry href attributes that are re-requested on later attribute access (resource.py:566/:589) - a genuine external input boundary for a library. Attacker controllability depends on the host's webhook endpoint exposure; kept for conservative recall.

token is interpolated into 'recurly_js/result/%s' (js.py:42): the fixed non-scheme prefix guarantees a relative reference, so urljoin(recurly.base_uri(), ...) keeps the host at the operator-configured *.recurly.com base. Path-only control.

Invocation inside the module's if __name__ == '__main__' demo block (line 95 prints parse_link_value(sys.argv[1])): not part of the library runtime and not an untrusted boundary; the live call is resource.py:153 (labeled separately).

Public classmethod: the full request URL is supplied by the caller and flows directly into Resource.element_for_url(url) -> http_request. The untrusted boundary is the embedding application; no validation exists between this parameter and the network.
Public classmethod: the full request URL is supplied by the caller and flows into Resource.headers_for_url(url) -> http_request(url, method='HEAD'). Boundary = embedding application.

Vendored Link-header parser call: propagates the server-controlled Link header value into pagination URLs (Page.start_url / next_url, resource.py:154-158) that next_page/first_page re-request. A taint propagation step, not a sink.

label.rationale: The only request funnel: every library request passes http_request(url, ...) -> urlsplit(url) (line 240) -> HTTP(S)Connection(urlparts.netloc) (lines 245/247/250) -> connection.request(method, url, ...)
